A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KBQA-o1 and contain 23 readable pages, including Appendices A–K. Text and visual comparison establish complete correspondence; pages 3–8 and 12–23 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on GrailQA, WebQSP, and GraphQ, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and quantified error analysis in Section 5 and Appendix J.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity studies, and appendix error analysis.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A, C, and E retain the same ReAct agent, eight query tools, policy and reward models, MCTS procedure, and incremental fine-tuning.

E1.justification: Both versions use GrailQA, WebQSP, and GraphQ over Freebase, including GrailQA's i.i.d., compositional, and zero-shot evaluations. Section 5.1 and Appendix D contain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain identical comparator membership and missing-result entries. Section 5.4 retains RG-E2E, GR-E2E, CoT-SbS, and ToT-SbS. Removing the Interactive-KBQA citation from related work does not remove an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices D and G retain the same 40-shot GrailQA and 100-shot WebQSP/GraphQ protocols, splits, sample counts, metrics, model configurations, and training/search settings.

E4.justification: Table 5's five component ablations, Figures 4–5's operator, efficiency, and sensitivity analyses, and Appendices I–J's case study and error analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three randomly seeded experiments. The existing plus/minus uncertainty reporting in Tables 2–5 and error bars in Figure 5 are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are identical, including appendix results. For example, Llama-3.1-8B F1 remains 78.5 on GrailQA, 59.8 on WebQSP, and 48.7 on GraphQ in Tables 2–4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–43, Propositions 4.1–4.3, Appendix B proofs, and Appendix C complexity analysis are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about heuristic KBQA, reduced annotation dependence, low-resource performance, and generalization. The claim to the first heuristic KBQA method is also retained.

C2.justification: The Impact Statement is shortened, but its detailed future directions remain in unchanged Appendix K. Reward-model limitations and failure explanations remain in Appendix J, while Section 5's interpretations are identical.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, Algorithm 1, dataset statistics, Table 7 hyperparameters, the eight-A40-GPU disclosure, and public code access information are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgments add no implementation details.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Wang et al. (2024) on temporal knowledge graph reasoning and removes Xiong et al. (2024, Interactive-KBQA) and Trinh et al. (2024, AlphaGeometry). It also drops AlphaGeometry and GPT-o1 as MCTS application examples, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording reductions in Related Work and the Impact Statement, adds funding acknowledgments, and adds an ICML 2025 publication notice. The remaining narrative and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page publication notice and page 9 acknowledgments cause local text and bibliography reflow. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–7, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding and publication disclosures and modestly condenses prose, while slightly revising related-work coverage. These edits improve administrative completeness but do not materially change readability, scientific support, or reproducibility. The methods, evidence, proofs, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful net quality difference.
